purpose: Rules about the data format and scoring scope. Prepended to every criterion prompt, so criterion files stay pure checklist content and can be swapped.
rules: Only operator messages are scored. The operator sees the full client–bot exchange, so bot and system messages are known context (details already given, verification events, chat closure).
Tokens in square brackets such as '[Имя скрыто]' or '[Персональные данные скрыты]' are masked real content: treat them as present, never as missing or as an error.
For channel 'voice call' the transcript is speech-recognition output: misheard words, garbled phrases and fragmented turns are transcription artefacts, not operator mistakes.
System messages may be in RU, KZ or EN; interpret them by meaning.

Messages marked 'internal' happened while the client was on hold (consultation with colleagues); the client did not hear them. Never score them as communication with the client (contact, empathy, dialogue_management, gross_errors). They may be used only as context for what the operator knew (consultation).
Cite evidence by message index [i] and timestamp with a short quote.
preprocessing_in_code: Parse both timestamp formats (MM:SS for chats; ISO-8601 with 7-digit fractions for voice — truncate to 6).

Voice calls: move the end-of-call system event ('Клиент завершил разговор' etc.) to the end of the transcript — it is logged before the last utterance(s) because of ASR latency. Keep original indices for evidence.
Index messages as '[i] timestamp speaker: text'.
Drop the constant bot boilerplate (AIM greeting, privacy notice).
Voice calls: mark every non-system message between the 'client on hold' and 'no longer on hold' events as speaker 'internal'.
Merge consecutive same-speaker fragments in voice calls, keeping original indices.
Compute mid-dialogue operator reply gaps and pass them as hints for dialogue_management.
